title: Henry Zeno and Henry Martin
summary: He and Russell discuss the drummer Henry Zeno, whom he says is really Henry Martin.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: There were a few of the other drummers uptown, you remember a fellow by the name of Henry Zeno.
Henry Zeno, I forgot all about him, I'm glad you mentioned him, Henry Zeno, yeah. Then we had Red, Red Duga. Yes, I never knew Henry.
Yeah, you heard of Red Duga.
Let me see, Henry Zeno, I forgot, that's Parade Man and a dance man. Henry Zeno. Henry Martin, is that the name?

Good drummer, good drummer. He played a while, before you run out, when we, Pierron Brookerby's old band, and they formed a band, they called it the Creole Serenade, with Peter Volcar and Dwight Newman and Charlie and Henry, they had six pieces, Henry Zeno was their drummer. I forgot about that.
Some call him Henry Martin, some say Henry Zeno, but he's right name, Henry Martin.
I thought they were two different fellas, but did they not?
No, no, Henry Martin, that's right, Henry Martin, you know, slim, bronziker looking fella, yeah, I forgot about him. Always smoked sigils. Then you had, uh, I met their mother once, uh,
Yeah. Kept the school, she was the caretaker of a school up there.
